entries.submitted_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: a StarlitCoffee Learn recognition icon, displayed at 48-52 dp inside an existing 68 dp tonal badge.
Input roles: Image 1 is the real equipment photograph, for anatomical construction only. Image 2 is the SHIPPED StarlitCoffee Learn icon family, the exact visual language to extend. Images 3 and 4 are individual shipped Clever and automatic-drip icons, for line weight, compact form, muted materials, glass treatment, and shading. Do not reproduce the contact sheet, labels, badges or other equipment. Deliver one icon only.
Primary request: extend that existing illustrated family with the requested brewer. Match the reference icons' softly illustrated, compact, simplified dimensional appearance. Muted periwinkle planes, dark navy outlines, warm ivory rim and restrained brown coffee accent. Essential readable equipment parts, modest soft highlights, matte/satin finish. Keep glass almost clear/ivory like the Clever, not bright blue. Preserve the photo's mechanical anatomy while simplifying its small textures and controls to the reference icons' detail level.
Avoid a new visual style: no shiny chrome product render, luminous bright blue glass, mirror-metal reflections, bright white specular streaks, elaborate machining, oversaturated blue, dramatic studio light, realistic photo texture or tiny control labels. Do not make the object more reflective or complex than its neighboring shipped icons.
Composition: same front three-quarter view and modest view into open tops as the existing family. Exactly one complete object, compact silhouette, centered with 8 percent clear margin on all sides. All handles, feet, lids and spouts fit. No ground shadow, scene, cup, hand, action, badge, border, letters, numbers, logo, watermark, checkerboard or background. Genuine transparent alpha.

Method: French press. Representative anatomy: Bodum Chambord 1928.
Equipment: Cylindrical glass jug in a simple metal frame, curved black side handle, short pour spout, domed lid, round plunger knob and central straight rod leading to a visible mesh disc inside the jug. Use the Chambord photograph's silhouette and support feet.
Exclude: No V60 cone, separate filter basket, extra mug, kettle, printed markings, or steam.

Equipment: One generic covered wide-mouth glass steeping jar with a simple screw lid, rounded shoulders, broad cylindrical body, and dark coffee-colored contents well below the lid. Exclude: No retail carton, cluster of jars, embossed lettering, measuring marks, integral filter basket, ice, straw, serving tumbler, spigot, or capacity claim.

Edit the AeroPress icon in Image 1 with one anatomical correction. Image 2 is the real AeroPress Original equipment photograph. Images 3, 4 and 5 are the shipping StarlitCoffee Learn family and individual Clever/batch style references.
Preserve the current icon's composition, muted transparent plastic, navy outlines, compact simplified illustration, lower chamber, filter cap, spacing and actual transparent background.
Correct only the top of the emerging piston: the AeroPress plunger has a CLOSED flat press surface across its broad top flange. The candidate mistakenly shows an open hollow oval. Fill that top with a solid flat dark navy press plate, seen as a shallow oval in this angle, with one modest soft periwinkle highlight. The upper piston must be clearly distinct from the lower brewing chamber. Do not add an open rim, hole, handle, long rod, lid knob, mug, lettering, numbers, logo, bright glare, badge or scene. Exactly one fully assembled upright AeroPress, all flanges inside the existing safe margins, genuine transparent alpha.
